In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ATPase from A. niger was a proton-translocative ATPase, acid-phosphatase and alkalaine-phosphatase.
the ATP-degrading system of A. nigger is composed of three enzymes, namely, ATPase, acid and alkaline phosphates, which act in series.

the A. niger acid phosphatase is a typical acid phosphatase which has a broad specificity for various phosphomonoesters, is activated by Mg2+, Mn2+ and Ca2+ and inhibited by Na+, NaF, HgCl2, Na3VO4 and Na2MoO4.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ATPase, acid and alkaline phosphates of A. nigger were able to hydrolyze the three phosphate moeities of ATP in a sequential manner.
the ATPase, acid and alkaline phosphates are the enzymes responsible for ATP degradation by A. niger.
the A. niger acid and alkaline phosphates are the major enzymes involved in the degradation of ATP to AMP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ATPase and alkaline and acid phosphatases are involved in ATP hydrolysis in A. niger.
the three phosphate-hydrolysing enzymes of A. nigel could be involved in the hydrolysis of ATP molecule.
the ATPase of A. nigger is unique as it is active at pH 2, is easily solubilizable in distilled water and its activity is not affected by addition of Na+, Ca2+ or K+ to the reaction mixture.
